```plato
    //==
    // # Rational Bezier curves
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve#Rational_B%C3%A9zier_curves
    // De Casteljau is linear in its control values, so running it on the
    // weighted points gives the numerator sum(B_i w_i P_i) and running it on
    // the weights alone gives the denominator sum(B_i w_i).

    // The point on a rational Bezier curve at t. Precondition: the weight sum
    // at t is non-zero.
    Eval(self: RationalBezierCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.ControlPoints.Count
                .MapRange(i => self.ControlPoints[i].PositionVector * self.Weights[i])
                .DeCasteljau(t)
            / self.Weights.DeCasteljau(t))
           .ToPoint;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Composite Bezier curves
    //
    // The canonical parameter is split evenly across the segments: segment i
    // covers [i / count, (i + 1) / count]. Each segment evaluates through the
    // CubicBezier2D / CubicBezier3D Eval in `library CurvesShapes`.

    // The point on a chain of cubic Bezier segments at t.
    Eval(self: CompositeBezier2D, t: Number): Point2D
    {
        var n = self.Segments.Count;
        var i = (t * n.ToNumber).Floor.ToInteger.Clamp(0, n - 1);
        return self.Segments[i].Eval(t * n.ToNumber - i.ToNumber);
    }
```

```plato
    // The point at the given unit parameter: the basis-weighted sum of the
    // control points.
    Eval(self: BSplineCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D {
        var domain = self.ParameterDomain;
        var u = KnotParameter(domain, t);
        var sum = self.ControlPoints.Count.Range.Reduce(Vector2D.Zero, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.ControlPoints[i].PositionVector
                * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        return (sum.X, sum.Y);
    }
```

```plato
    // The point at the given unit parameter: the weighted basis sum divided by
    // the summed weights, which is the projection back out of homogeneous space
    // that makes a NURBS curve rational — and lets it represent conics exactly.
    Eval(self: NurbsCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D {
        var domain = self.ParameterDomain;
        var u = KnotParameter(domain, t);
        var count = self.ControlPoints.Count;
        var numerator = count.Range.Reduce(Vector2D.Zero, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.WeightedControlPoint(i)
                * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        var denominator = count.Range.Reduce(0.0, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.Weights[i] * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        var p = denominator == 0.0 ? numerator : numerator / denominator;
        return (p.X, p.Y);
    }
```

## Line 323

```plato

    // The point on a piecewise cubic Hermite spline at t: the Hermite segment
    // spanning the two knots that bracket t, with their explicit tangents.
    Eval(self: HermiteSpline2D, t: Number): Point2D
    {
        var n = self.Points.Count;
        var i = n.SpanIndex(self.Closed, t);
        var u = n.SpanFraction(self.Closed, t);
        return self.Points.AtWrapped(i, self.Closed).PositionVector
            .Hermite(self.Points.AtWrapped(i + 1, self.Closed).PositionVector,
                     self.Tangents.AtWrapped(i, self.Closed),
                     self.Tangents.AtWrapped(i + 1, self.Closed),
                     u)
            .ToPoint;
    }
```

## Line 352

```plato

    //==
    // # Evaluating the interpolating splines
    //
    // Evaluation of the curves declared in `splines.types.plato`:
    // Catmull-Rom, Kochanek-Bartels (TCB), piecewise-linear, and the accessors of
    // the natural cubic spline. The cubic bases themselves live in
    // `library Polynomials` (`polynomials.types.plato`), generic over `INumerical`, and the
    // piecewise indexing helpers (SpanCount / SpanIndex / SpanFraction / AtWrapped)
    // in the sections above; nothing is reimplemented here.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * A chain of n points has n - 1 spans when open and n when Closed (the
    //     last point joins back to the first).
    //   * Control points are converted to displacements with PositionVector before
    //     entering a `INumerical`-generic basis function and back with ToPoint, the
    //     explicit point/vector converters from `library Transforms`.

    //==
    // # Catmull-Rom splines
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_Hermite_spline#Catmull-Rom_spline
    //
    // TODO(cross-package): only the UNIFORM (Alpha = 0) parameterization is
    // evaluated here, because `library Polynomials` provides the uniform basis.
    // Centripetal / chordal Catmull-Rom (Alpha = 0.5 / 1) needs knot spacings
    // proportional to the chord lengths raised to Alpha, i.e. a non-uniform
    // Hermite whose tangents are rescaled per span; that belongs next to the
    // basis in `polynomials.types.plato`, not here. Until it lands, `Alpha` is
    // documentation rather than behaviour.

    // The point on a Catmull-Rom spline at t, uniform parameterization.
    Eval(self: CatmullRomCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D
    {
        var n = self.Points.Count;
        var i = n.SpanIndex(self.Closed, t);
        var u = n.SpanFraction(self.Closed, t);
        return self.Points.AtWrapped(i - 1, self.Closed).PositionVector
            .CatmullRom(self.Points.AtWrapped(i, self.Closed).PositionVector,
                        self.Points.AtWrapped(i + 1, self.Closed).PositionVector,
                        self.Points.AtWrapped(i + 2, self.Closed).PositionVector,
                        u)
            .ToPoint;
    }
```

```plato

    // The point on a TCB spline at t: the Hermite segment between the bracketing
    // knots, with the departing tangent of the first and the arriving tangent
    // of the second.
    Eval(self: TcbSpline2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.Points.AtWrapped(self.Points.Count.SpanIndex(self.Closed, t), self.Closed)
               .PositionVector
               .Hermite(self.Points
                            .AtWrapped(self.Points.Count.SpanIndex(self.Closed, t) + 1,
                                       self.Closed)
                            .PositionVector,
                        self.TcbOutgoingTangent(
                            self.Points.Count.SpanIndex(self.Closed, t)),
                        self.TcbIncomingTangent(
                            self.Points.Count.SpanIndex(self.Closed, t) + 1),
                        self.Points.Count.SpanFraction(self.Closed, t))
               .ToPoint;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Piecewise-linear splines

    // The point on a piecewise-linear spline at t: a straight lerp within the
    // span bracketing t.
    Eval(self: LinearSpline2D, t: Number): Point2D
    {
        var n = self.Points.Count;
        var i = n.SpanIndex(self.Closed, t);
        return self.Points.AtWrapped(i, self.Closed)
            .Lerp(self.Points.AtWrapped(i + 1, self.Closed),
                  n.SpanFraction(self.Closed, t));
    }
```

## Line 675

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/splines.library.plato, line 675](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/splines.library.plato#L675).

```plato

    // The value at the given unit parameter, mapped onto the spline's own
    // parameter domain. Outside [0, 1] the parameter clamps rather than
    // extrapolating: a natural spline is linear beyond its ends, and returning
    // that continuation silently would hide a caller's mistake.
    Eval(self: NaturalCubicSpline1D, t: Number): Number
        => self.KnotCount < 2
            ? self.KnotValue(0)
            : self.SpanValueAt(self.ParameterDomain.Lerp(t.Clamp(0.0, 1.0)));
```
